key_insight: CAM-B3LYP accurately captures pentacene–fullerene charge-transfer excitation energies, closely matching an optimally tuned range-separated hybrid reference, while B3LYP and DFTB substantially underestimate them.
engineering_relevance: For organic photovoltaic interface design, the choice of electronic-structure method strongly affects predicted exciton and charge-transfer energetics, making range-separated hybrids preferable for screening donor–acceptor complexes.
method: Compared four pentacene–buckminsterfullerene interface models with different donor–acceptor geometries.
Computed local excited states and charge-transfer states using TDDFT with CAM-B3LYP, B3LYP, and DFTB.
Benchmarked results against an optimally tuned long-range corrected functional (OPT-wB97XD).
evidence_signal: Across all four models, CAM-B3LYP produced charge-transfer energies very close to OPT-wB97XD, whereas B3LYP and DFTB were about 1 eV too low.
watch_item: The reported accuracy depends on interface configuration and functional choice, so lower-cost methods may give misleading energetics for charge-transfer screening.
paper_title: Local and Charge-Transfer Excitation of Pentacene-Buckminsterfullerene complexes
